datasets.name: Northlight Retail
datasets.description: Fictional Yorkshire retail chain: 5 stores, 20 products, 60 customers, 450 orders, Jan 2025 – Oct 2026. Ships a v_sales reporting view.

samples.label: Orders per store
samples.sql:
SELECT s.store_name, COUNT(*) AS orders
FROM orders o
JOIN stores s ON s.store_id = o.store_id
GROUP BY s.store_name;

samples.label: Revenue share by category
samples.sql:
WITH category_revenue AS (
  SELECT p.category,
         SUM(oi.quantity * p.unit_price * (1 - oi.discount)) AS revenue
  FROM orders o
  JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
  JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id
  GROUP BY p.category
)
SELECT category, ROUND(revenue, 2) AS revenue,
       ROUND(100.0 * revenue / SUM(revenue) OVER (), 1) AS contribution_pct
FROM category_revenue
ORDER BY revenue DESC;

datasets.name: Home Store
datasets.description: Online retailer, 2025: 50 customers, 30 products, 10 campaigns, 200 orders and 500 order lines.

samples.label: Orders per campaign
samples.sql:
SELECT c.CampaignName, c.Channel, COUNT(o.OrderID) AS OrderCount
FROM Campaigns c
LEFT JOIN Orders o ON o.CampaignID = c.CampaignID
GROUP BY c.CampaignName, c.Channel
ORDER BY OrderCount DESC;

samples.label: Revenue share by category
samples.sql:
WITH CategoryRevenue AS (
  SELECT p.Category,
         SUM(oi.Quantity * oi.UnitPriceAtSale * (1 - oi.DiscountRate)) AS Revenue
  FROM Orders o
  JOIN OrderItems oi ON o.OrderID = oi.OrderID
  JOIN Products p ON oi.ProductID = p.ProductID
  WHERE o.OrderStatus = 'Completed'
  GROUP BY p.Category
)
SELECT Category, ROUND(Revenue, 2) AS Revenue,
       ROUND(100.0 * Revenue / SUM(Revenue) OVER (), 1) AS ContributionPct
FROM CategoryRevenue
ORDER BY Revenue DESC;

datasets.name: Shopping
datasets.description: Small shop, 2023: 6 customers, 8 products, 50 orders and 20 new order quantities.

samples.label: Spending per customer
samples.sql:
SELECT c.CustomerName, COUNT(o.OrderID) AS OrderCount,
       ROUND(SUM(o.Total), 2) AS TotalSpent
FROM customers c
LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.CustomerID = c.CustomerID
GROUP BY c.CustomerID, c.CustomerName
ORDER BY TotalSpent DESC;

samples.label: Value of each new order
samples.sql:
SELECT q.NewOrder, p.ProductName, q.Quantity,
       ROUND(q.Quantity * p.UnitCost, 2) AS OrderValue
FROM quantities q
JOIN products p ON p.ProductID = q.ProductID
ORDER BY OrderValue DESC;
